title: Errors, logs and metrics
idea: Error handling turns each expected failure into a typed exception with a stable code; logging records what happened; monitoring counts outcomes so trends become visible.
points: Expected failures are unchecked `BookingException` subclasses with a stable `code()`.
Callers branch on `code()`, never on the message text, which may change.
Log one line per event with `key=value` fields, so tools can search them.
A counter per outcome shows trends a single log line cannot, like rising refusals.

code.title: Codes, log lines, counters
code.caption: The service is trimmed from the last page so the error handling stands out. Teams log through SLF4J with Logback.

walk.text: The base exception is unchecked and forces every subclass to supply a `code()`.
Each failure type keeps a fixed code; the message is for humans only.
Validate the slot first, then check overlaps in the same room; each failure throws its own type.
The caller catches the base type once, logs it and counts it by code.
One line per event: level, event name, then `key=value` fields.
A `TreeMap` keeps counter names sorted, so the summary prints the same every run.

pitfalls: Do not catch and log the same exception at every layer; log once at the boundary.
Never branch on `getMessage()` text; branch on `code()`, which you promise to keep.
Keep personal data out of logs; log ids such as `E7`, not names or emails.

quiz.q: What does the last line print?
quiz.why: Only 9-10 books. 9.5-11 and 9-9.5 overlap it; 12-12 ends where it starts. `TreeMap` sorts upper-case keys before lower-case ones.

takeaway: Typed exceptions with codes, one structured log line, a counter per outcome.

starters: Should BookingException be checked or unchecked, and why?
How would these error codes map to HTTP status codes in a REST API?
What should I put in an alert, and what only in a dashboard?
